procedural_history.originating_court: Trial Court in respect of FIR no. 0030 of 2021 registered at P.S. Sadar, Gurugram; Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Thalassery, Kerala in FIR No. 53 of 2020 registered at P.S. Pinarayi, Kerala.
procedural_history.impugned_order: Bail orders in FIRs other than FIR no. 0030 of 2021 registered at P.S. Sadar, Gurugram and FIR No. 53 of 2020 registered at P.S. Pinarayi, Kerala.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: Not mentioned in the provided text.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The petitioner approached the Supreme Court by filing a Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 149 of 2024, seeking a direction that the personal bond and surety already furnished in one case be treated as sufficient for other bail orders as well. The Supreme Court allowed the writ petition.

directions: The writ petition is allowed in terms of the directions given hereinabove.

issue.issue_text: Is the petitioner entitled to the relief of treating the personal bond and one set of sureties already furnished as holding good for the other bail orders also?

facts: The petitioner was accused in 13 different FIRs across 6 states.
Although he was granted bail in all 13 cases, he remained in custody because he was unable to find and furnish separate sureties for each case as required by the individual bail orders.
The petitioner had already furnished a personal bond and sureties in two of the cases.
He argued that his inability to produce multiple sureties was preventing him from exercising his liberty, despite the bail orders.
law: The purpose of requiring sureties is to ensure the presence of the accused at trial.
The court must balance the requirement of furnishing sureties with the accused's fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
An order that protects the person's fundamental right under Article 21 while also guaranteeing their presence is considered reasonable and proportionate.
The specific nature of such an order depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.
application: The Court recognized that the petitioner was facing a "genuine difficulty" in finding multiple sureties, which effectively nullified the bail orders he had been granted.
The Court reasoned that this situation implicated his fundamental rights under Article 21, as his liberty was being curtailed despite having been granted bail.
To resolve this, the Court sought a "reasonable and proportionate" solution that would both secure the petitioner's presence for trial and protect his liberty.
The Court rejected the State's argument that a separate surety is required for each individual case.

Instead of a single bond for all cases, the Court devised a state-wise solution. For the FIRs pending in each state (Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, and Uttarakhand), the petitioner was required to furnish only one personal bond and two sureties.
This single set of bonds and sureties within a state would be considered valid for all the FIRs registered against him in that particular state.
Crucially, the Court also allowed the "same set of sureties to stand as surety in all the States," directly addressing the petitioner's inability to find numerous different people to act as sureties.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the petitioner's plea and granted relief. It modified the bail conditions by directing that for each state where FIRs were pending, the petitioner would furnish one personal bond and two sureties, which would hold good for all cases within that state. Furthermore, the same two individuals were permitted to act as sureties across all the different states, thus resolving the petitioner's inability to furnish multiple sureties and enabling his release.

arguments.issue_text: Is the petitioner entitled to the relief of treating the personal bond and one set of sureties already furnished as holding good for the other bail orders also?
appellant_arguments: The petitioner argued for a modification of the bail conditions, requesting that a single personal bond of Rs. 30,000 and one set of two sureties for the same amount should be deemed sufficient to cover all 31 cases against them.
The petitioner also sought to be relieved from the direction to produce a local surety.
respondent_arguments: The provided text does not contain the specific arguments made by the respondents.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A court may relieve a petitioner from the direction to produce a local surety.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Keeping the principles discussed hereinabove, we direct that for the FIRs pending in each of the States of Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab and Uttarakhand, in each State, the petitioner will furnish his personal bond for Rs. 50,000/- and furnish two sureties who shall execute the bond for Rs. 30,000/- each which shall hold good for all cases in that state. This is based on the precedent that imposing a bail condition which is impossible to comply with would defeat the very object of release.
legal_tests_applied: In Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. (2022) 10 SCC 51, this Court held that “imposing a condition which is impossible of compliance would be defeating the very object of release.”
policy_considerations: One of the reasons which delays the release of the accused/convict is the insistence upon local surety – In such cases, the courts may not impose the condition of local surety.
In the present case, the petitioner hails from Haryana and to secure a local surety will be an arduous task for him – This condition virtually rendered the order for bail ineffective.
